legend: You are given n$$$n$$$ intervals [li,ri]$$$[l_i,r_i]$$$, where li≤ri$$$l_i \le r_i$$$. Your task is to determine if there exist n$$$n$$$ integers x1,x2,…,xn$$$x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$$$ satisfying:
li≤xi≤ri$$$l_i\le x_i \le r_i$$$ for all 1≤i≤n$$$1 \le i \le n$$$;
input: The first line contains an integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$), the number of test cases.
The first line contains an integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤105$$$2 \le n \le 10^5$$$) denoting the number of intervals.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers l1,l2,…,ln$$$l_1, l_2, \ldots, l_n$$$ (1≤li≤106$$$1 \le l_i \le 10^6$$$).
The third line contains n$$$n$$$ integers r1,r2,…,rn$$$r_1, r_2, \ldots, r_n$$$ (li≤ri≤106$$$l_i \le r_i \le 10^6$$$).
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 105$$$10^5$$$.
output: YES if it is possible to choose x1,x2,…,xn$$$x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$$$ such that it satisfies the constraints. On the next line, output n$$$n$$$ space-separated integers x1,x2,…,xn$$$x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$$$.
The letters in the word YES and NO are case insensitive. For example, YES, yeS and No are all considered valid.
note: In the first example, we choose 5$$$5$$$, 5$$$5$$$ and 10$$$10$$$ respectively from each range. Then, we have gcd(5,5,10)=5≠1$$$\operatorname{gcd}(5,5,10) = 5 \neq 1$$$.
In the second example, it is not possible to choose n$$$n$$$ integers satisfying the condition.
